method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 48 draws only Ave R 1/2 (west edge) and Ave S; sheet 60 draws Q, Q 1/2, R and R 1/2 (east edge), so R 1/2 is the only shared corridor, and both crops print its name - 'AVENUE R 1/2' at the left margin of sheet 48 (with neighbour sheet number 66 beside it) and 'AVENUE R 1/2' at the right margin of sheet 60 (with neighbour sheet number 48 beside it). The street-address runs settle the block: sheet 48's block SE 138, east of the avenue, carries the 2400 runs '2401 2403 2405 2407 2409 2411 / 2413 ... 2423' on 31ST ST and '2402 2404 ... 2412 / 2414 ... 2424' on 32ND ST, while sheet 60's block NW 140, west of the avenue, carries the 2300 runs '2301 2303 2305 2307 2309 2311 / 2313 ... 2323' and '2302 2304 ... 2312 / 2314 ... 2324'. The 2300/2400 hundred-block change happens across this one avenue. Avenue frontages face odd-to-even as expected: sheet 48's west column reads 3101,3103,...,3127; sheet 60's east column reads 2802,2804,...,2828. Corridor is 70 ft (printed '70' mid-avenue on both) against 80 ft cross streets; centres read off the green native rulers since detection's candidates (436 / 2777) both fall inside blocks.
